findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, which is not a real CSS property (IE10's vendor syntax is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted on the previous line). The declaration is silently dropped by every CSS parser, so the line is dead code that misleads future maintainers into thinking IE legacy coverage exists for `align-items` when it does not; anyone debugging IE alignment will waste time on a line that never had an effect.

[ADVISORY] The flexbox()/order() mixins emit 2009-spec properties (`display: -webkit-box`, `-moz-box`, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, `-moz-box-ordinal-group`) alongside a plain `order` on a flex container, but the 2009 and modern `order`/`box-ordinal-group` semantics differ such that `-moz-box` support requires paired `-moz-box-orient`/`-moz-box-direction` declarations that this mixin never emits. On legacy Firefox builds that honor `-moz-box`, the header layout falls back to source-order box layout without direction/orient, producing a horizontally vs vertically stacked header that differs from the intended flex row; support staff debugging old-browser header breakage will trace it to these half-specified 2009 declarations.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits a nonexistent `-ms-align-items` property; the only valid IE10 prefix is `-ms-flex-align`, which is already emitted two lines earlier. Every consumer of align-items ships a dead declaration that is dropped by the IE10 parser; harmless functionally but signals the mixin set was written without verification against the old-flexbox syntax it targets, and the next editor will copy the pattern.

[ADVISORY] The avatar-to-text clearance in .small-action was switched from a fixed 4em left padding to `padding: 0 1.5%`, a percentage of the flex container width, while the avatar itself keeps its fixed pixel sizing. On narrow/mobile-width topic lists the gap between avatar and description shrinks proportionally (1.5% of ~340px ≈ 5px vs the previous 4em ≈ 48px), so the uppercase description text visually collides with or crowds the avatar for anyone viewing small-action posts (topic closed, whisper notices) on phones.

[ADVISORY] Making `.small-action` a flex container turns every descendant element between `.topic-avatar` and `.small-action-desc` into a flex item, and the removed `margin-top: 5px` / `padding-top: 4px` compensations were the only vertical spacing on the non-legacy code path. Small-action variants whose DOM includes additional direct children (extra buttons, custom theme/plugin inserts) get laid out in a single centered row with no spacing between items, breaking theme-component overrides of small-action that relied on block/float layout; no mobile stylesheet counterpart in this diff was audited for the same change.

[ADVISORY] The `.panel` relies on `@include order(3)` with old-spec `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`/`-moz-box-ordinal-group` prefixes, but only `.extra-info-wrapper` in topic.scss got `order(2)` while `.title` (the first flex child in the header `.contents`) has no explicit order, so visual ordering on old-2009-flexbox browsers depends entirely on DOM order. On browsers honoring the 2009 flexbox spec (older Android/BlackBerry WebKit that Discourse's prefixed output targets), the header panel's ordinal group of 3 without siblings 1 and 2 assigned makes its position implementation-defined, so logged-in and logged-out header controls render in the wrong slot for those users.

[ADVISORY] The small-action change goes beyond a layout-mechanism swap into unrelated visual redesign: replacing `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` with `padding: 0 1.5%`, dropping `margin-top: 5px`, collapsing `.small-action-desc p { margin: 5px 0 }` to `0`, and removing `padding-top: 4px` on `> p`. Any regression in small-action (moderator notices, closing posts) vertical rhythm is untraceable to the stated flexbox/layout intent and will be misattributed; whoever bisects a spacing bug lands on a PR labeled 'performance' with no requirement covering the new padding/margin values. Percentage padding also makes the gutter viewport-dependent, changing appearance on narrow screens with no spec'd target.

[ADVISORY] `line-height: 1.5` added to `.extra-info-wrapper` is a typographic change with no traceability to the 'optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins' intent, and the removal of `.bullet { margin-top: 5px }` is a spacing change beyond the mechanism swap. Header title/badges text rendering changes for all users without any requirement or visual-signoff trail; a later spacing regression here will be blamed on the flexbox refactor even though it came from an unrelated line-height edit in the same diff.

[ADVISORY] The new mixins emit `-moz-box` / `-moz-inline-box` (2009-era Flexbox with no `box-*` companion properties) and `-ms-align-items` (a property that never existed in any IE release), so portions of every mixin output are dead declarations. Every future stylesheet that includes these mixins ships non-parsing `-moz-box`/`-ms-align-items` lines plus real 2009-spec `-webkit-box` output; because these mixins are foundation-level, the drift compounds across the codebase, and the missing `box-align`/`box-pack` companions mean old-WebKit browsers silently get no alignment, not the mixin's promised behavior.

[ADVISORY] Making `.small-action` a flex container with `align-items(center)` is applied unconditionally, but `.small-action` is a generic wrapper used by many non-header posts (close notices, custom small-action plugin outputs), so this diff re-layouts element types well outside the stated header scope. Plugin/theme components that emit `.small-action` markup assuming block flow with avatar float get re-laid-out in topics everywhere, not just headers; regressions there will surface as core bugs from a PR whose stated intent was header performance.

[BUG] Converting .contents to a flex container without flex-wrap breaks the header's overflow behavior: flex items default to nowrap, so a long .title truncates/squeezes the .panel and .extra-info-wrapper onto one shrunken row instead of wrapping as the old float layout did. On topics with long titles on narrow viewports, the title text overflows or compresses the panel (hamburger/avatar) because nowrap flex items shrink to min-content rather than dropping to the next line like floated elements did.

[BUG] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment`, which is not a real property in any browser, alongside the correct `-ms-flex-align`. The line is dead code that every stylesheet bundles; the next editor copying this mixin pattern propagates the phantom property and may believe IE10 support comes from it, when in fact only the separate -ms-flex-align line does anything.

[BUG] Right-aligning .panel via `margin-left: auto` only works under the standard flexbox spec; in the 2009 old-spec engines the same mixin enables (`display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box`), auto margins do not pack items — the old spec requires -webkit-box-pack — so .panel sits immediately after the title instead of flush right on old WebKit/Firefox builds the mixin explicitly targets. Users on the legacy-flexbox browsers this mixin set claims to support (old Android WebKit, Firefox <22) get the panel glued to the title with no right alignment, a visual regression versus the removed `float: right` which worked everywhere.

[ADVISORY] The flexbox mixins stack five mutually exclusive display values plus four generations of prefixed alignment/order properties in one rule, relying on each engine's last-supported-wins behavior rather than scoping prefixes per engine generation. A browser that understands -webkit-box but also the unprefixed order takes a mix of 2009 and standard properties; any future property added to these mixins must be re-verified against all four spec generations, and the invalid `-ms-align-items` line shows that verification is not happening.

[ADVISORY] The visual order of header children is now encoded as scattered magic integers across separate files — .extra-info-wrapper gets order(2) in topic.scss, .panel gets order(3) in header.scss, and .title silently relies on the default 0 — so no single location describes the header's child sequence. The next contributor adding a header element (or reordering) must discover and coordinate magic numbers in two stylesheets plus the implicit default; picking an order of 1 or 2 for a new element silently displaces the existing children's intended sequence.

[ADVISORY] .small-action was made a flex container while its child `.small-action-desc` lost the `4em` left indent and now relies on flex layout alone; any non-flex rendering context (browsers with flex disabled, print stylesheets reusing these classes) loses all indentation since the padding that provided the fallback was deleted rather than kept as a non-flex baseline. Small-action rows (e.g. closed-topic notices, user deletions) render with the description text jammed against the avatar edge in non-flex contexts, and the change also removes the margin-top that separated multi-line descriptions.

[ADVISORY] Setting `.small-action` to `align-items(center)` applies vertical centering to every descendant including the custom-action buttons inside `.small-action-desc`, changing alignment of action buttons that the old padding-based layout positioned at the top. Small-action entries whose description contains a button (e.g. topic closing with a reopen button) get the button vertically centered relative to the avatar, a visual shift for all small-action content not considered by this diff.

[BUG] Making .contents a flex container silently disables the float:right layout of every other header child while only .panel was migrated, so any sibling that still relies on floats (search, hamburger, notifications in classic Discourse markup) loses its right alignment because floats are ignored on flex items. Users see header controls stack left-to-right in DOM order after deploy instead of the right-aligned layout the previous design specified — the visual objective of the header is changed without any markup migration in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The PR's stated objective is header layout performance, but the same diff restyles .small-action topic content (padding 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em -> 0 1.5%, margin-top removal, p margin/padding zeroing), silently widening the accepted objective to a redesign of topic-stream small actions. Reviewers accepting 'header performance' approve an unreviewed visual redesign of topic close/merge notices; anyone bisecting a topic-page regression later finds it hiding in a header PR.

[ADVISORY] Deleting the .bullet { margin-top: 5px } compensation inside .extra-info-wrapper changes the vertical alignment of bullet-style category badges with no replacement alignment rule, altering the pre-existing rendered header appearance rather than preserving it. Themes and sites using the bullet category style see badges sit 5px lower relative to the title text after deploy — a silent visual regression outside the 'performance optimization' intent.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, which is not a valid property in any browser (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, already emitted on the line above), so it is dead code that misleads future readers into thinking IE10 support requires it. The next maintainer copying this mixin pattern propagates the invalid property into new mixins, and the duplicated -ms-flex-align ordering bug (ms-flex-align before ms-align-items suggests intended distinct prefixes) is hidden by the dead line.

[BUG] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a valid property in any IE version — IE10/11 recognize only `-ms-flex-align` (already emitted on the line above), so this declaration is always discarded as a parse error and silently does nothing. Harmless in practice for IE10/11 (the correct -ms-flex-align line covers them), but it signals a copy-pasted old syntax and anyone relying on `-ms-align-items` for old-IE alignment gets a silent no-op with no console error; dead declaration also inflates every stylesheet that includes the mixin.

[ADVISORY] .contents now sets `display: flex` via the mixin, which changes the children that previously relied on block layout — including .valign-helper and .panel internals — so any descendant text node or element that is a direct child of .contents becomes an anonymous flex item, stripping text-node whitespace and changing vertical alignment/baseline behavior. Users on the header page get visibly shifted titles/valign-helper text in browsers where the old float layout was expected; the regression is silent because CSS cannot error — it only mis-renders, and the diff ships with no visual-spec coverage of the header contents layout.
